text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London made fresh gains and nearby months finished the day at session's peak, helped by a run-up in New York and worries over cold weather in Brazil's coffee belt. Front month July added $67 to close at $1,890 per tonne. September closed $75 higher at $1,925 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York ended sharply higher as weather forecasts called for another chilly night in Brazil. Even though no damage was forecast, the market reacted strongly. July closed 16.05 cents/lb higher at 253.30 cents/lb, while September added 9.45 cents/lb to close at 223.60 cents/lb. The outer months added between 7.25 and 9.00 cents/lb. Traders said that although Brazil's coffee regions escaped damaging cold this past week, reports of frost in low-lying areas where no coffee is grown were enough to rattle nerves with memories of two severe frosts three years ago still fresh.

GUATEMALA - Guatemala exported 406,026 60-kg bags of coffee in May which compares to 574,634 bags exported the previous month. That brought total exports for the year so far up to 3.784 million bags, which is in line with earlier expectations.

POLAND - Poland imported 162,100 bags of coffee in January 1997, 10 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 5.8 percent to 1.624 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January 1997 were Peru (18,100 vs 12,500 bags), Indonesia (45,000 vs 27,300 bags) and Vietnam (27,100 vs 19,500 bags). Exports in January 1997 reached 10,300 bags, up from 2,800 bags exported the same month the previous year. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose to 88,200 bags from 42,300 bags in 1995.

NEW ZEALAND - New Zealand imported 42,300 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, 5.5 percent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 9 percent to 162,900 bags. The main supplier of green coffee in January/March 1997 was Vietnam with 12,600 bags, up from 9,900 bags shipped the same period in 1996.
